title: The Implications of Client-Centered Therapy for Family Life
coreMove: Convert a family demand into a relationship condition that makes honest self-direction more possible.
sourcePressure: Rogers moves the client-centered stance into family life, where acceptance and control collide in intimate daily decisions. No split source sidecar exists for ch16; frozen TOC and book skeleton support the heading, part placement, and broad intent only, with no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Mistaking acceptance for permissive parenting or conflict avoidance.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.
